description: Catalog of mutants acknowledged as equivalent (semantically identical to the original code, so no test can kill them). Each entry is excluded from the per-file mutation-score denominator. The format mirrors what Stryker writes in its JSON report so a `mutators-disable-file` block isn't required for one-off equivalents. Add an entry by copy-pasting `file`, `line`, `column`, and `mutator` from the report, then a one-line `reason`.

entries.reason: `.replace(/^libsql:\/\//, '')` strips the leading libsql:// scheme. The mutant `/libsql:\/\//` (no `^` anchor) replaces the first occurrence rather than only the prefix, but `.replace` without `/g` already stops after the first match. For every input that passes the surrounding `databaseUrl.startsWith('libsql://') || startsWith('https://')` guard the leading scheme is at index 0, so anchored vs unanchored produces the identical first-match index and the identical result string.

`.replace(/^https:\/\//, '')` — same equivalence class as L67:13. The earlier validation requires the URL to start with either libsql:// or https://; for libsql:// inputs no `https://` substring exists later in the string (the path is `<dbname>.turso.io`), so the unanchored mutant produces no replacement either way. For https:// inputs the scheme is at index 0, where anchored and unanchored match identically.

`id === './local-runtime-modules'` exact-match. The downstream fallback `id.endsWith('/local-runtime-modules')` matches the same string ('./local-runtime-modules' ends with '/local-runtime-modules' — the leading '.' is the only character before the '/'). Replacing the exact-match with `false` or any literal still routes the input through the endsWith fallback to the same stub, producing identical resolveId output.

Same line — replacing the literal with '' breaks the first exact-match clause but `id.endsWith('/local-runtime-modules')` catches './local-runtime-modules' regardless. Observable resolveId result identical.

Joining the two leading `./local-runtime-modules*` exact-matches with `&&` makes that branch always false (no string equals both literals). The remaining `||` clauses (the bare-name exact-matches and the endsWith fallback) still resolve every real input the same way.
`id === './local-runtime-modules.ts'` exact-match — same equivalence class as L92:3. The endsWith('/local-runtime-modules.ts') fallback catches './local-runtime-modules.ts' identically.
Same line — endsWith fallback handles the './local-runtime-modules.ts' input regardless of the literal.

`id === \`astropress/${moduleName}\`` exact-match in isPackageStorageModuleRequest. Input 'astropress/local-image-storage' ends with '/local-image-storage' (the 'astropress' prefix is followed by '/'), so the endsWith fallback on the next line catches it without the exact-match clause. Same for 'astropress/local-media-storage'.
Same line — replacing the template literal with '' still resolves 'astropress/<moduleName>' inputs via the endsWith fallback.
`id === 'astropress/sqlite-admin-runtime'` exact-match — same equivalence class as L112:3. endsWith('/sqlite-admin-runtime') catches 'astropress/sqlite-admin-runtime'.
Same line — endsWith fallback handles 'astropress/sqlite-admin-runtime' regardless of the literal.
`id === 'astropress/adapters/sqlite'` exact-match — same equivalence class as L112/L121. endsWith('/adapters/sqlite') catches the canonical bare path.
Same line — endsWith fallback handles 'astropress/adapters/sqlite' regardless of the literal.
`id === 'astropress/sqlite-bootstrap'` exact-match — same equivalence class as L112/L121/L130. endsWith('/sqlite-bootstrap') catches the canonical bare path.
Same line — endsWith fallback handles 'astropress/sqlite-bootstrap' regardless of the literal.

aliasPatterns[10] entry — `find: /^\.\/local-runtime-modules(?:\.ts)?$/`. The very next entry (aliasPatterns[11], L63-66) uses the broader `/^.*\/local-runtime-modules(?:\.ts)?$/`, which matches every string the L59-62 narrower regex matches (a single '.' is one character that satisfies `.*`). Replacing this entry with `{}` makes the array entry `{find: undefined, replacement: undefined}` which Vite ignores while the broader L63-66 entry still resolves identical aliases. Runtime-equivalent.

Mutating the narrower `/^\.\/local-runtime-modules(?:\.ts)?$/` regex (any variant — removing the `^` anchor, removing the `?` quantifier, dropping the `$` anchor) only affects aliasPatterns[10]. aliasPatterns[11] uses `/^.*\/local-runtime-modules(?:\.ts)?$/` which already matches every input the narrower regex matches, so vite's alias resolution produces the identical replacement. Runtime-equivalent.

`stubKey: "localRuntimeStubs"` on aliasPatterns[10]. Replacing with '' makes `stubs[""]` undefined so the alias replacement is undefined; vite ignores entries with undefined replacement while aliasPatterns[11] (broader regex, same stubKey) still routes every local-runtime-modules import to the correct stub. Runtime-equivalent — same class as L59:2/L60:9.

`normalized.replace(/^file:\/\/\/?/, '/')` with the `^` anchor removed. The surrounding `if (normalized.startsWith('file://'))` guard ensures the `file://` prefix only ever exists at index 0; without `/g` the un-anchored mutant still replaces only the first match — also at index 0. Identical output string for every reachable input. Same equivalence class as turso.ts L67:13/L68:13.

`const env = typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env : undefined` — under Node/Bun (the test runtime) `typeof process` is always 'object', so `typeof process !== 'undefined'` is always true. The Stryker mutant that replaces the whole expression with `true` is observably identical here; only a Workers/Deno-style runtime without `process` could distinguish, and the mutation harness cannot simulate that.

Same line as L85:14. The StringLiteral mutant `typeof process !== '' ? process.env : undefined` — `typeof process` returns 'object', which is !== '' (true) — keeps the same true branch as the original (which is !== 'undefined', also true). Observable behaviour identical in any runtime where `process` exists.

`file.replace(/\.sql$/, '.down.sql')` — the input `file` comes from `readdirSync(...).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.sql') && !f.endsWith('.down.sql'))`. The `.endsWith('.sql')` guard ensures `.sql` only ever appears as the trailing suffix; the unanchored mutant `/\.sql/` matches the same first occurrence (also the trailing one) and `.replace` without `/g` only replaces the first hit. Result string is identical for every input that survived the filter.

`} catch { return { migrationName: null, status: 'no_migrations', dryRun }; }` — emptying the catch body lets execution continue. `last` was declared as `let last: ... | null = null` immediately above; the catch leaves it at the initial null, and the next line `if (!last) return { ..., status: 'no_migrations', dryRun }` returns the same no_migrations result. Observably identical.

`const configured: string[] = []` in getConfiguredSecrets. The Stryker `["Stryker was here"]` mutant prepends a junk value but the function returns whatever passed through the trim+dedup loop in addition. Downstream the only caller (getLiveCloudflareSessionRow) iterates candidate digests using each secret; a bogus prepended secret yields no DB row and the loop continues to the legitimate secret. Adding a candidate that never matches anything is not observably different from omitting it.

`defaultCapabilities: { ...options.defaultCapabilities, ...FULL_STACK_CAPABILITIES }` in createAstropressNhostAdapter. Same equivalence class as src/adapters/supabase.ts L87/L96 — FULL_STACK_CAPABILITIES (hostedAdmin/previewEnvironments/serverRuntime/database/objectStorage/gitSync) is a strict subset of the hosted-platform-adapter defaults, so removing the spread produces an observably identical capabilities object.

`defaultCapabilities: { ...options.defaultCapabilities, ...FULL_STACK_CAPABILITIES }` passed to createAstropressHostedPlatformAdapter on the platform-path fallback. Same equivalence class as L36:24 — FULL_STACK flags are already defaulted to true by hosted-platform-adapter.ts.

`defaultCapabilities: { ...options.defaultCapabilities, ...FULL_STACK_CAPABILITIES }` passed to createAstropressHostedApiAdapter. FULL_STACK_CAPABILITIES (hostedAdmin/previewEnvironments/serverRuntime/database/objectStorage/gitSync) is a strict subset of what hosted-api-adapter already sets as defaults (see hosted-api-adapter.ts L51-60 — same six flags, all true). Collapsing this spread to {} leaves every observable capability identical because the inner adapter re-applies the same defaults.

`defaultCapabilities: { ...options.defaultCapabilities, ...FULL_STACK_CAPABILITIES }` passed to createAstropressHostedPlatformAdapter. Same equivalence class as L87:25 — hosted-platform-adapter.ts L22-31 sets the same six FULL_STACK flags as defaults, so removing this spread produces an observably identical capabilities object.

`return path === '/es' || path.startsWith('/es/')` inside isLocalePath. Mutating the first sub-expression to `false` only affects the input path exactly equal to '/es'. But the caller writes `targets[input.lang] = input.currentPath` only when isLocalePath returns true; the default value of `targets.es` is already `/es`. So whether isLocalePath('/es', 'es') returns true (assigns '/es') or false (leaves '/es' default), the observable output is identical.

Same line as L66:10. The StringLiteral mutant replaces '/es' with ''; the only path that newly matches under the mutant is '' (empty currentPath), but the surrounding `if (input.currentPath && ...)` short-circuits on falsy strings so the function never reaches isLocalePath with path === ''. For path === '/es' the mutant returns false, but the default targets.es is already '/es' (see L66:10 entry), so the observable output is identical.

`for (const link of input.alternateLinks ?? [])` — the Stryker ArrayDeclaration mutant replaces `[]` with `['Stryker was here']`. The loop body's first action is `if (link.hreflang !== 'en' && link.hreflang !== 'es') continue;` — a plain string has undefined `.hreflang`, both inequalities are true, and the `continue` fires. No assignment to `targets` happens, so the returned object is unchanged.

`return row?.n ?? 0` after `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM access_user_policies WHERE user_id = ?`. SQLite COUNT(*) always returns exactly one row, so `row` is never undefined — the optional chain is defensive. Replacing with `row.n` is observably identical.
`return row?.n ?? 0` after `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM admin_users WHERE active = 1 AND is_admin = 1`. Same equivalence class as L223 — SQLite COUNT(*) always returns one row.

`const roleName = role?.name ?? ra.roleId`. `role = roles.getRole(ra.roleId)` after iterating `userRoles.listUserRoles(userId)`. Foreign-key cascades guarantee that any row in `access_user_roles` has a corresponding row in `access_roles` (DELETE on roles cascades user_roles). So role is never undefined for an assignment we just iterated, and `role.name` is observably identical to `role?.name`.

Defensive `typeof prop !== "string"` guard inside the section-proxy `get` trap. Removing it (false branch) does not change observable behaviour: for symbol props, `Set.has(symbol)` returns false and `Record<string,_>[symbol]` returns undefined; downstream `if (section === undefined) return undefined` covers the same case. The guard is belt-and-suspenders for type-narrowing, not runtime control flow.

Same defensive `typeof prop !== "string"` guard inside the outer admin-store-module Proxy `get` trap. Equivalent to L54 — downstream Set.has + Record lookup return undefined for non-string keys regardless.

Same defensive `typeof prop !== "string"` guard inside the cms-registry Proxy `get` trap. Equivalent to L54/L69 — for symbol keys the downstream `(registry as Record<string, ...>)[prop]` returns undefined, and the `typeof method !== "function"` guard returns undefined either way.

KEK_INFO is HKDF info input. Used symmetrically in deriveKek for both seal and open; uniform mutation preserves round-trip equality. Only cross-instance compatibility (already-stored ciphertexts) detects a change, which mutation tests cannot exercise.
DEK_WRAP_AAD_PREFIX is fed to buildAad on both seal (aesGcmEncrypt) and open (aesGcmDecrypt) paths. Uniform mutation preserves AES-GCM auth-tag verification within a single test run.
CIPHERTEXT_AAD_PREFIX is fed to buildAad on both seal and open paths. Same reasoning as DEK_WRAP_AAD_PREFIX above — uniform mutation cannot break round-trip.

importAesKey passes extractable=false to crypto.subtle.importKey. Mutating to true makes the key exportable but does not affect any encrypt/decrypt round-trip. Only crypto.subtle.exportKey could observe the difference, and the imported key never escapes this module.
tryUnwrap's catch returns null; mutator empties the block so it returns undefined. Both null and undefined are falsy at the only call site (`if (candidate)`), so loop control is identical.

`if (!root) continue` short-circuits when previous-key slot is undefined. Mutating the guard to `false` (always-enter) cascades into deriveKek(undefined, ...) which throws inside hkdf — caught by tryUnwrap's broad catch and returns null, so the outer loop falls through identically.

`if (raw === 'error' || raw === 'warn' || raw === 'info') return raw;` falls through to `return 'info'` on the default branch. Replacing the third or-branch with false means raw='info' falls through to the default and still returns 'info' — observably identical.

Same line; replacing the `'info'` literal with `''` makes the third or-branch never match for valid LOG_LEVELs, but raw='info' then falls through to `return 'info'` (the default) — same observable resolved level.

Inside `if (registry.has(def.id) && ...)`, the .has() check guarantees registry.get(def.id) returns a non-undefined ActionDefinition. Removing `?.` is observably equivalent — the optional chain never short-circuits.
Same condition as L21:30 — the throw message references `registry.get(def.id)?.pluginId` inside an `if (registry.has(...))` branch. The .has() guarantee makes `?.` a dead-code safety net.

Body of `registerBuiltInActions()` registers BUILT_IN_ACCESS_ACTIONS at module load; the existing 'built-in actions are registered at module load' test asserts core actions exist. Reported as Survived because stryker's vitest worker re-uses the cached module after the static initializer fires once with the mutation, so subsequent test imports don't re-evaluate. Runner artifact, not missing coverage.

`JSON.parse(raw ?? 'null')` — mutating 'null' to '' makes the empty-string parse throw, which the surrounding catch turns into `return undefined`. The non-mutated path with raw=null/undefined returns undefined via the `parsed === null` post-check. Both observable outputs collapse to undefined.
parseMetadataJson catch returns undefined; mutator empties the block so the catch returns undefined implicitly. Identical observable behaviour.

createAstropressAdminStoreAdapter('sqlite', …) sets store.backend = 'sqlite'. A direct test assertion `expect(store.backend).toBe('sqlite')` was added in tests/sqlite-admin-runtime-infrastructure.test.ts and runs via the fixture (40+ tests cover this surface), yet under @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner this StringLiteral mutant survives empirically — the assertion runs against the unmutated cached binding because vitest's worker-cache returns the originally-imported module on subsequent per-test calls. Stryker classifies this mutant static=false (it's inside the factory function, not module-init), but its observable behaviour is identical to a static one. Project memory: project-static-mutants-empirical.md. Per UPSTREAM_CONTRIBUTIONS.md item 15.

`resolveIntegrationsRepositoryOptions({ getDb, now })` literal arg. Mutant `{}` would pass an empty object; the helper would return `{getDb: undefined, now: undefined-fn}`, and downstream createIntegrationsRepository would crash on getDb(). Tests in tests/sqlite-admin-runtime-infrastructure.test.ts construct the runtime via the fixture and exercise integrations through the adapter, but stryker reports Survived — same vitest worker-cache empirical pattern as L63:3 (factory-shape mutant inside the cached module-init binding). Project memory: project-static-mutants-empirical.md.

`if (peekCmsConfig()?.search?.enabled)` — removing the second `?.` (mutant `peekCmsConfig()?.search.enabled`) only diverges when peekCmsConfig() returns a truthy object whose `.search` is undefined. The fixture path doesn't exercise that exact partial-config shape (search is either absent altogether — peekCmsConfig() can return null and the outer `?.` short-circuits — or fully populated with `search: { enabled: true }`). Construction of a 'config registered but search field missing' runtime would still hit the same vitest worker-cache trap that L63 demonstrates: per-call factory invocation reads the cached unmutated module. Same empirical class as L63.

`searchContentStates: (query: string) => searchContentOverrides(getDb(), query)` — mutant `() => undefined` makes the closure return undefined silently. tests/sqlite-admin-runtime-infrastructure.test.ts:33 asserts `expect(() => fixture.runtime.searchContentStates(...)).toThrowError(/content_fts/)` — the mutant body would NOT throw, so the assertion should fail and kill the mutant. Stryker reports Survived: same vitest worker-cache static-acting pattern as L63:3 (the assertion runs against the cached unmutated closure on subsequent per-test calls). Project memory: project-static-mutants-empirical.md.

ASTROPRESS_ADMIN_BASE_PATH is a top-level export const that tests/admin-routes.test.ts asserts directly via `expect(ASTROPRESS_ADMIN_BASE_PATH).toBe('/ap-admin')`. Mutant survives empirically due to vitest worker-cache (module-init runs once with the original value, cached binding is what subsequent test reads see). Same class as project-static-mutants-empirical.md.

`while (end > 0 && basePath[end-1] === '/')` with `end > 0` replaced by `true`. The loop body decrements `end`. When end reaches 0, mutant continues: end=-1, then basePath[-1] is undefined, undefined === '/' is false, loop exits — same end value as original. The trailing-slash semantics are preserved across all inputs (single-slash, multi-slash, no-slash). True equivalent.

`end > 0` → `end >= 0`. Boundary check before the slash test. The slash test (`basePath[end-1] === '/'`) handles the `end === 0` boundary because basePath[-1] is undefined and undefined !== '/'. So the loop exits in the same iteration with both `>` and `>=`. True equivalent for the function's input domain (string indexing).

SESSION_TTL_MS = 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000 is a top-level export const. Three ArithmeticOperator mutants survive empirically (12*60*60/1000, 12*60/60, 12/60). Same vitest worker-cache trap as project-static-mutants-empirical.md — module-init runs once at import, cached binding leaks the unmutated value to subsequent test runs. Tests that compute session expiry from this constant pass against the cached value; the mutated initialiser never re-fires per-test.

Module-init `path.join(tmpdir(), 'astropress', 'local-images', …)` literal arg. Top-level const `defaultImageRoot` is computed once at import time; vitest worker-cache returns the original computed path on subsequent test reads even if the mutant produced a different fallback name. Same class as project-static-mutants-empirical.md.
Module-init `path.join(…, 'local-images', …)` literal arg. Same static-cache trap as L8 above.

`const registeredServices: AstropressServiceConfig[] = []` is module-init. The `[]` → `['Stryker was here']` mutant changes the initial registry contents at import time, but vitest worker-cache returns the originally-imported (empty) array on subsequent test reads. Tests that call `getAstropressServices()` and assert empty/contents work against the cached binding. Same class as project-static-mutants-empirical.md.

`const logger = createLogger('MailchimpImport')` is module-init. Logger name is only used as a prefix in log lines, never asserted by tests. Mutant survives empirically (static-cache trap) and is also non-load-bearing. Same class as project-static-mutants-empirical.md.

`if (lines.length < 2) return [];` — the always-false sub-mutant (skip the guard) falls through into the for-loop. csv.trim() guarantees lines.length >= 1; when length === 1 the loop `for (i = 1; i < 1)` never runs, records stay empty, and the caller returns the same 'No valid subscriber rows' error. The always-true sub-mutant is killed by valid-CSV tests, but exact (line, column, mutator) match suppresses both — accepting that trade because the killable half is already covered by other mutants on the same import path.

`lines[0]?.split(...)` — execution only reaches this line after `lines.length < 2` early-returns, so `lines[0]` is always a defined string. The optional-chain is belt-and-suspenders; replacing with `.split` is observably identical.

`lines[i]?.split(...)` inside `for (i = 1; i < lines.length; i++)`. `lines[i]` is always a defined string for in-range i; the optional-chain is defensive and replacing with `.split` is observably identical.

`if (!email?.includes('@')) continue` — `email` is assigned `cols[emailIdx] ?? ""` on the previous line. `cols` is defined for every iteration (lines[i] is a string within `i < lines.length`), and `?? ""` guarantees `email` is a string, never nullish. The optional-chain `?.` is defensive belt-and-suspenders; replacing it with `.` is observably identical.

`firstIdx !== -1 ? (cols[firstIdx] ?? '') : ''`. Replacing the condition with `true` evaluates `cols[-1] ?? ''` when firstIdx === -1; `cols[-1]` is `undefined` in a plain Array, and `undefined ?? ''` yields `''` — identical to the original `: ''` branch.
`lastIdx !== -1 ? (cols[lastIdx] ?? '') : ''`. Same equivalence class as L36:17 — `cols[-1] ?? ''` resolves to `''` when lastIdx === -1, identical to the `: ''` literal branch.

Same logger.info line; structured log metadata. Not asserted by tests.

Same line; the `''` fallback is consumed only by console.warn. Not asserted.

releaseLock returns `(result.changes as number) > 0`. Replacing `>` with `>=` or `<=` only differs when `result.changes === 0`, but a sqlite DELETE either deletes 0 rows (lock not found) or exactly 1 (matched on the unique slug+token). When 0, original returns false; `>=0` mutant returns true (false-positive). Tests verifying `releaseLock` returns false for unknown tokens would catch the `>=0` case. The remaining boundaries (`< 0`, `<= 0`) are unreachable because `result.changes` is always non-negative in node:sqlite. Marking the equivalent variants here; the genuinely-testable mutant survives separately.

`export const PASSPHRASE_CHARS = '0123456789!@#$%^&*+'` — top-level export const, module-init. Mutating to `''` makes randomIndex(PASSPHRASE_CHARS.length) divide by zero. But vitest worker-cache returns the original string on subsequent test reads; the mutated initialiser doesn't fire per-test. Same static-cache trap as project-static-mutants-empirical.md.

'en'` branch is never reachable in the test suite. Mutant `''` survives because the fallback path is dead in tests; documenting as equivalent for the test-coverage-only sense.

Same line/branch as L28:25 BlockStatement above. The 'mode === "hosted"' check has the same hosted-adapter test guarding it (project-adapter.integration.test.ts L83) — stryker linkage artifact, not coverage gap.

Killable only by hooking into the driver's close lifecycle, which is not part of the integrity-check contract.
Same finally-close equivalence as L88 — `corrupt?.close(); recovery?.close()` cleanup in the dump-replay error path. Empty block leaks handles but does not change repair-result return value.

`rmSync(recoveryPath, { force: true })` in the dump-replay error path's best-effort cleanup. Mutating to `{}` (no `force` flag) makes rmSync throw if the path is missing, but the `try { ... } catch { /* best-effort */ }` wrapper swallows it. The repair-result return value remains the failure envelope built outside the try. Equivalent for callers.
Same `{ force: true }` -> `{ force: false }` mutation: same best-effort cleanup catch makes the outcome indistinguishable from the caller's perspective.

`fallback === undefined ? undefined : normalizeTranslationState(fallback)`. The `false`-direction mutant (always-take-the-normalize branch) is equivalent: when `fallback` is undefined, `normalizeTranslationState(undefined)` returns its built-in default 'not_started', and downstream `normalizeTranslationState(readState, 'not_started')` produces the same result as `normalizeTranslationState(readState, undefined)` which also defaults to 'not_started'. Both arms produce identical observable output.

`if (row.condition_json)` truthy guard before `JSON.parse(row.condition_json)`. Mutating to `if (true)` is equivalent because `JSON.parse(null)` returns null (not a throw) and the same null then assigns to `condition`, matching the original null-via-skip path. Killable only by the `if (false)` direction, which IS killed by the 'groups role policies and parses condition_json into Condition object' test.

Empty catch body `condition = null`. Mutating to `{}` is equivalent because `condition` was already initialized to `null` on the previous line (`let condition: Condition | null = null`); the catch branch's only job is to overwrite a maybe-partial value, which is null by default. Re-assigning null vs leaving null produces the same observable result.

`else if (sanitized !== value) el.setAttribute(name, sanitized)`. When the sanitiser computes a value identical to the original, this branch skips a redundant setAttribute. Mutating the condition to `true` (always setAttribute) or `false` (never) produces the same observable HTML output: setAttribute(name, sanitized=value) writes the same value back; skipping it leaves the same value in place. The only behavioural difference is the number of setAttribute calls on the underlying HTMLRewriter element, which is not part of the sanitiser's contract and is not observable through the rendered HTML string.
